findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, so the feature flag is dead and the check is misleading
findings.body: The function computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false on both branches of the `if`. The result is always false, so SQL expressions are rejected whether or not the `sqlExpressions` flag is on. The flag check is dead code. The error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is also wrong for operators who have deliberately enabled the flag: they get a message that suggests the feature is missing rather than disabled for security reasons. A maintainer reading this will not see that the disable is intentional. Make the disable an explicit constant or a clearly commented early return, with an error message that says the feature is disabled for security reasons.

findings.title: TablesList now always fails, so existing tests of SQL parsing are likely broken or unchanged
findings.body: After the change, `sql.TablesList` calls the stub `DB.RunCommands`, which always returns 'not implemented'. Every call to `TablesList` therefore returns an error. The PR changes no test files. Any existing parser or SQL command tests that expect table names from a valid query will fail, and nothing in the diff updates or removes them. The rest of the function (the quote escaping and the JSON AST flattening) is now unreachable in practice. Either remove or skip those tests with a clear reason, or add tests that assert the disabled behaviour.

findings.title: Stub DB type and NewInMemoryDB look like a working in-memory database
findings.body: `DB` and `NewInMemoryDB` are exported from package `sql` and used as if they were a real engine, but every method returns 'not implemented'. `TablesList` on the stub is never called by the new code. Nothing in the file says this is a deliberate disable placeholder. A future caller could reasonably assume it works, and the 'not implemented' errors are surfaced to users as generic 'error reading SQL command' bad requests, which hides the real reason. Add a comment explaining the stub and why it exists.

findings.title: Hashes for thrift, asmfmt, minio and others are moved from go.sum to go.work.sum
findings.body: The diff removes `h1:` hashes for `apache/thrift v0.20.0`, `klauspost/asmfmt`, `minio/asm2plan9s`, `minio/c2goasm`, and `google/go-replayers` from go.sum and adds them to go.work.sum. The module graph is not otherwise changed. This suggests the lockfile was regenerated under a workspace, not with `GOWORK=off`. Anything that builds without the workspace (for example a downstream module importing grafana/grafana, or CI with GOWORK=off) may fail with missing checksum errors if those modules are still required. The go.mod removals (go-duck, thrift, go-which, orderedmap) should be checked against `go mod tidy` run with GOWORK=off so the dependency files agree.

findings.title: Feature-flag documentation still describes SQL expressions as usable
findings.body: The PR leaves the `sqlExpressions` flag registered and documented, but after this change the flag no longer enables anything. Operators who read the docs and turn the flag on will get a failing SQL expression with no explanation in the docs. The PR description defers the docs update, but at minimum the doc should say the feature is disabled for this security release, so operators are not misled.
